references.text: The creation account in [ref:Gen 1:1-3|Genesis 1:1-3] describes how God created the heavens and the earth by his word. John connects the Word (Logos) directly to creation, showing that all things came into being through him—the same creative Word that was in the beginning.

In [ref:Gen 1:26|Genesis 1:26], God says, "Let us make mankind", where the plural form suggests a joint action within the Godhead. This points to the Word's role as co-creator, as expressed in John 1:3.

[ref:Ps 33:6|Psalm 33:6] states: "By the word of the Lord the heavens were made, all their host by the breath of his mouth." This confirms that everything was created by God's word, which John identifies with Christ.

[ref:Ps 33:9|Psalm 33:9] says: "For he spoke, and it came to be; he commanded, and it stood firm." God's creative word brings all things into existence, consistent with the truth that all things were made through the Word in John 1:3.

[ref:Ps 104:24|Psalm 104:24] praises God's diverse creation made with wisdom. This wisdom associated with creation is understood in light of John 1:3 as the Word who was active in all that was created.

In [ref:Prov 8:22-30|Proverbs 8:22-30], Wisdom speaks of her role at creation: "When he established the heavens, I was there." This personified wisdom has clear parallels to the Logos/Word in John 1:3, through whom all things were created.

In [ref:Isa 44:24|Isaiah 44:24], the Lord says that he is the one who created everything. John 1:3 identifies the Word with this act of creation and emphasizes that nothing came into being without him.

Paul writes in [ref:1 Cor 8:6|1 Corinthians 8:6] that "for us there is ... one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom all things exist." This is a direct parallel to John 1:3 and confirms Christ's role as the one through whom all things were created.

In [ref:Col 1:15-17|Colossians 1:15-17], Christ is called the firstborn over all creation, and it is said that "all things were created through him and for him ... in him all things hold together." This expands on John 1:3 and shows Christ's role in both creation and sustenance.

In [ref:Heb 1:2-3|Hebrews 1:2-3], it is stated that God has spoken to us through the Son, "through whom he also created the world." This directly confirms that the Son, the Word, is the one through whom all things came into being, in agreement with John 1:3.

[ref:Heb 11:3|Hebrews 11:3] says that "by faith we understand that the universe was created by the word of God." Here, God's creative word is linked to faith and points back to the Word's role in creation as described in John 1:3.
In [ref:Rev 3:14|Revelation 3:14], Christ is called "the beginning of God's creation." This title confirms his role in creation, as emphasized in John 1:3—that all things came into being through him.
